sources.name: §16i SGB II — Teilhabe am Arbeitsmarkt
sources.coverage: 100% years 1–2, then 90/80/70% years 3–5 of eligible subsidy basis
sources.important_limit: If employer is not bound by or references an applicable collective agreement, subsidy calculation uses statutory minimum wage as basis.
sources.training: Up to €3,000 required further-training costs during funded employment; in-company training can qualify.

sources.name: §16e SGB II — Eingliederung von Langzeitleistungsbeziehenden
sources.coverage: 75% year 1, 50% year 2 of regular remuneration for eligible employment

sources.name: Berlin complementary §16i funding
sources.coverage: For qualifying common-good employers, Berlin states it can top wage costs back to 100% from year 3 and provide an expense allowance; subject to available budget.

sources.name: Soziale Betriebe Berlin
sources.coverage: Berlin finances professional guidance and social-pedagogical support; projects may combine with §§16e/16i or other wage subsidies, with Berlin also describing degressive wage support where those are unavailable.

sources.name: ESF+ Berlin 2021–2027
sources.coverage: Berlin programme focuses on education, skills/workforce and social inclusion. Exact instrument rules must be checked before stacking.

sources.name: Maßnahme bei einem Arbeitgeber (MAG)
sources.coverage: Practical employer-based trial for eligible unemployed/jobseekers, subject to prior approval. It is not employment and the employer does not pay wages during MAG; OpenWork must never represent MAG as paid productive employment.

sources.name: LOTTO-Stiftung Berlin
sources.coverage: Project-specific public-benefit grants. Example: €325,000 for Silbernetz digital/social support project for older Berliners.

sources.name: Aktion Mensch — inclusion enterprise start-up funding
sources.coverage: For eligible inclusion enterprises/additional-income businesses: up to €300,000 and up to 90% of eligible costs under the current offer.

sources.name: Public procurement / service contract
sources.coverage: District, Land, public-company or other public buyer pays for a defined service/outcome. Exact procurement and tariff-compliance rules apply.

sources.name: Company / philanthropic mission buyer
sources.coverage: Private buyer fully or partially purchases a verified mission outcome or closes the fair-wage premium gap.
